query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum addition improves the oxidation resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer
generation.mechanism: Aluminum promotes the formation of a stable and protective oxide layer, reducing oxidation and improving resistance to high-temperature degradation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxidation resistance and maintained mechanical performance
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 600 °C to 1600 °C, atmosphere: air or oxidizing environment
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of aluminum addition and the resulting microstructure are uncertain

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aluminum-added HfNbTaTiZr exhibits significantly reduced oxidation resistance or degraded mechanical performance compared to the untreated material, the hypothesis is falsified.
